summary: King Chung Lo specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. Lo completed a PhD at Leipzig University, studying under doctoral supervisor Eli Franco in 2009.

King Pong Chiu specializes in Indology and religious studies. Chiu earned a Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Manchester under the doctoral supervision of Jacqueline Suthren Hirst (attested 2014).
Kisari Mohan Ganguli (1848–1908) was an Indologist. Ganguli studied at Presidency University, Kolkata, and the University of Calcutta.

Kisor Kumar Chakrabarti works in philosophy and Indology. Chakrabarti studied under teachers Gopinath Bhattacharyya, Ashoke Kumar Gangopadhyaya, and traditional teachers Madhusudana Nyayacarya, Visvabandhu Tarkatirtha, Narmada Tarkatirtha, Panchanana Sastri, and Narayana Chandra Gosvami Nyayacarya, later holding a post at the University of Calcutta.

Kitaro Nishida (1870–1945) was a philosopher and religious studies scholar educated at Ishikawa Normal School, Fourth Higher School, and Tokyo Imperial University. His academic posts included Fourth Higher School, Otani University, and Kyoto University, where he served as Professor of Philosophy (1912–1927).

Kiyoaki Okuda (born 1938) is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral research under Ludwig Alsdorf (~1968–1973). Okuda held posts as professor at Shitennoji University (attested 1993) and director of the Shitennoji Doctrinal Research Institute (attested 2000).

Kiyoshi Kato (1907–1956) was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Otani University under Enga Teramoto, earning a BA in 1931, and held posts at Higashi Honganji (1935) and Hyangsam Vocational Girls' School (1938).

Kiyoshi Okano (born 1956) is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who studied under Bhikkhu Pāsādika. Okano has held posts at Kyushu University as associate professor (attested 2002) and professor (attested 2013–2024).

Kiyoshi Shimokawabe (born 1944) is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral coursework at Rissho University. Shimokawabe also held appointments at Rissho University, attested in 1990 and as a special researcher in 2001.

Kiyotaka Kimura (born 1940) specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. Educated at Tokyo University of Education and the University of Tokyo, Kimura served as Professor Emeritus at the University of Tokyo, President of Tsurumi University (~2001–2011), and Professor at ICPBS (~2011).

Kiyotaka Yoshimizu specializes in Indology and philosophy, having studied under Gerhard Oberhammer (~1984–1989) and as a graduate student at the University of Tokyo. Yoshimizu held posts at Hokkaido University, Toyo Bunko, and as professor at Tohoku University (~2006–2020).

Kiyozo Kazama (born 1928) is a scholar of linguistics and Indology. Kazama studied at the University of Tokyo under Naoshiro Tsuji and at the University of Vienna, later holding posts at Hosei University, Nagoya University, and the University of Tokyo (~1970–1989).

Klaus Karttunen (born 1951) is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He earned his BA, MA, Lic.Phil., and PhD at the University of Helsinki, studying under Pentti Aalto and Asko Parpola, and later held various academic and research posts there.
Klaus Mylius (1930–2025) was an Indologist. Mylius held posts at Leipzig University (~1968–1992), the University of Bayreuth, and Goethe University Frankfurt (attested 2003).
Klaus Pinte works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. Pinte studied at Ghent University under Pol Vanden Broucke and served there as a teaching assistant in 2006.

Klaus Röhrborn (born 1938) is a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. Röhrborn held professorships at the University of Giessen (~1974–1993) and the University of Göttingen (~1993–2004).

Klaus Wille (born 1953) is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. Wille held posts at the University of Göttingen, the Austrian Academy of Sciences, and the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2000–2009 and 2018–2020).

Klaus-Dieter Mathes is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned degrees from Marburg and Hamburg, studying under Michael Hahn and Klaus Sagaster. Mathes held posts with the NGMCP, University of Hamburg, and University of Vienna (attested 2012–2013).
Klemens Karlsson specializes in religious studies and Buddhist studies. Karlsson studied under doctoral supervisor Peter Schalk and received a Doctor of Philosophy from Uppsala University in 2000.

Knut A. Jacobsen (born 1956) is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. After studying at the University of California, Santa Barbara (~1989–1994), he held professorships at the University of Bergen (~1996) and the University of Oslo (attested 1999).
